Files changed: generation-metadata.tex (revision timestamp and a third, derive-homily contribution; effort recorded as packet-declared high and host-dispatched xhigh, as this run's intervention records 0000 and 0001 state), research/production-review.md (Derive-homily section), and one comment line of proper-components.toml above the homily components (no declaration changed). Evidence re-read at this stage, none of it changing a research record: every Douay-Rheims verse quoted, in the tracked verse files; Augustine, Sermo 87.4, 6, 8, 10-11 and Chrysostom, Hom. in Matt. 64.3-4, in the tracked NPNF texts; Jerome, PL 26 col. 142, Aquinas on Matthew p. 262 and Aquinas on Isaiah p. 556, on the page images of the retained facsimiles; Augustine, Enarr. in Ps. 144.22, in a fresh verified-TLS fetch of the augustinus.it page into scratch space (same byte count and SHA-256 as the scope record gives), which remains that sentence's only witness and is so described in the note. Editorial decisions a reviewer should know: Scripture is spoken in the Douay-Rheims and the speech names that Bible before its first quotation, since the assembly hears the Lectionary's approved English, which is reproduced nowhere; no oration or antiphon is quoted, and the speech says what 'the antiphon the Missal sets at its entrance' says without asserting that it was sung, since another chant may replace it; each Father is credited only with what he says of his own passage, and the four cross-element connections (psalm's two words and the householder's two dealings; Paul adding hours; the keeping and the arriving inside the Collect's prayer; Communion as the second line and pledge of the one wage) are spoken with no name attached; Chrysostom's position that no one murmurs in the kingdom is quoted and the murmur applied to the hearers, not to the saved; Augustine's sentence that the saints differ in brightness stands beside the claim that the wage cannot be divided. Left to the studies: the first interpretation, the saying on first and last, the Alleluia verse with the Augustine-Chrysostom difference on Acts 16:14, the Prayer over the Offerings and both Communion antiphons. The body contains no anecdote, first-person experience, clerical identity, stage direction or recited prayer. The prose was rehearsed silently, not aloud: a 1,764-word first draft was cut to 1,482, one 57-word sentence and the Collect sentence were split, and 'requital' and 'denarius' are glossed where they first occur. Upstream observations for the homily reviewer (nothing repaired; not this stage's owner): research/interpretations.md and research/scope.md, declared references of the homily components, still carry the sentences named in the study review's standing observation (Chrysostom said to dispute Augustine's second step, among them); the homily does not use Acts 16:14 or that step and follows the accepted study. The studies cite Jerome's sentence on the wish that another receive nothing at PL 26, 141-142; on the page image it stands in col. 142, which the homily's note cites. No other upstream defect was met. Retained evidence, all inside the stage's scratch directory .scratch/claude-pc-s51/work/derive-homily-0000/: proof/ holds copies of the final PDF, .aux, .log, extracted text, six page rasters, the contact sheet and SHA256SUMS; beside it are the crops of the three facsimile pages read and the fetched augustinus.it page. This is author verification; the shared-timestamp three-document build and the independent visual review remain.
summary: Wrote the standalone homily of the Claude postconciliar Twenty-fifth Sunday in Ordinary Time, Year A, for an adult parish assembly: homily.tex, the spoken body (sections/homily/10-homily.tex) and the terminal note with References (sections/homily/90-note.tex). The Wage and the Giver preaches the study's third interpretation (the householder's reply as payment and gift, the evil eye, the wage as the giver himself) joined to the second (Chrysostom's two kinds of hearer, Augustine against delay), and joins the Gospel with Isaiah 55, Psalm 145 (144), Philippians 1, the Entrance Antiphon, the Collect, Communion and the Prayer after Communion, the Missal texts by description only. 1,482 spoken words, about 11.4 to 12.3 minutes by arithmetic at 130 to 120 words a minute, no timed or audible delivery claimed; author proof of 6 pages with a clean log; all thirteen homily-preflight checks, the artifacts check and the metadata check exit 0; no new source-dependent claim and no upstream file edited.
